paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery feed; also preference, responsive, consent, performance, privacy and memory conditions.
News section listing representing category and live-news navigation templates.
Representative current article and core reading journey, including rendered versus crawler content.

Authenticated account, paid checkout, settings depth and destructive account actions were not traversed because they require credentials or a purchase; their entry surfaces were still judged where visible.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the system color scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-scheme screenshot remains the same white and grey light palette as the default capture; the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule and computed color-scheme was normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide system-driven dark surface, text, control and media treatments.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not explicitly supported.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no preference treatment, while Lighthouse found a 3.91:1 text contrast failure in the install banner under the default palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast-safe control styles and bring default text contrast to WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use declarative View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS probe found no view-transition rules or API styling across the link-heavy news experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article and section navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not expose scroll-aware state.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll timeline or scroll-state treatment on a long 12,574 px homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state queries or a declarative progress indicator for the long feed.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the entire primary experience on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, listing and article screenshots all show a large consent modal covering the content before any interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a concise, balanced consent surface that preserves access to core content and offers an immediate reject choice.

findings.summary: The consent modal is an ad hoc dialog and has no light-dismiss path.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found a DIV with role=dialog rather than dialog/popover; the visible surface only offers advanced settings and proceed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with correct focus containment, Escape handling and an explicit dismiss or reject action.

findings.summary: Consent and advertising chrome dominate the initial viewport.
findings.evidence: The consent panel occupies most of the desktop viewport, while the crawler screenshot is largely header and a large ad slot rather than editorial content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent copy and reserve the first viewport primarily for editorial content.

findings.summary: The homepage forces a 1280 CSS-pixel viewport on mobile.
findings.evidence: The viewport meta is width=1280; a 360x800 capture is a tiny scaled desktop layout and layout metrics report innerWidth 1280 at the mobile condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and reflow the layout at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Repeated card components are not container-responsive.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules, while the homepage reuses cards across 620, 300 and 290 px columns and then scales the whole desktop canvas on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards containment and size-aware styles instead of relying on the fixed page viewport.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small or have no visible custom focus.
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured 11.6x18 and 12 px-high buttons, 36 px icon links, and no outline on the search input and login button.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch areas and consistent :focus-visible rings.

findings.summary: The homepage purpose is weakened by an empty primary heading and blocking consent wall.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found an empty H1 and the first-view screenshot hides the editorial hierarchy behind consent text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a meaningful H1 or equivalent page heading and let editorial content establish purpose before secondary prompts.

findings.summary: Reading the selected article requires clearing the same blocking consent wall.
findings.evidence: The representative article screenshot shows its headline and body disabled beneath the full consent dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow article reading with a non-blocking consent choice and retain user context through the decision.

findings.summary: The initial consent state lacks a clear immediate decline or return path.
findings.evidence: The modal presents advanced settings and a high-emphasis proceed action, but no equivalent reject-all, close or back-to-content action.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose clear accept, reject and customise actions with equal clarity and preserve the underlying reading state.

findings.summary: Lab LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.2 s and Speed Index 6.4 s; the independent trace measured LCP 2.37 s, showing a condition-sensitive performance risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the editorial LCP resource and defer consent, ad and analytics work until after critical content.

findings.summary: Third-party startup work delays interactivity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 200 ms TBT and 23.4 s Time to Interactive, despite the separate trace recording no long tasks in its capture window.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential analytics, ad and paywall scripts and break remaining startup tasks into priority-scheduled chunks.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large and fragmented critical load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 262 requests and 3.81 MB transferred, including 28 stylesheets and parser-inserted high-priority Google Fonts and livebar CSS candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, self-host or rationalise fonts, cache static assets and defer below-the-fold integrations.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 603 KiB unused JavaScript and 40 KiB unused CSS; major waste comes from ads, Piano, tag managers and app bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising, paywall and analytics modules conditionally and split bundles by visible feature.

findings.summary: Important controls and embedded content lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed navigation links, an untitled livebar iframe and a visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch; the search input probe also found no label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every link, iframe and input a programmatic name that matches visible text.

findings.summary: Some small text fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the install banner at 3.91:1 against a required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the banner foreground or background token to meet at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark and focus structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The homepage H1 is empty, the probe found only header and footer landmarks in its DOM slice, and search/login controls showed no visible outline when focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a meaningful H1 and main landmark, then apply consistent :focus-visible styling to all interactive controls.

findings.summary: Mobile text is rendered as a scaled desktop page.
findings.evidence: The 360 px screenshot shows the fixed 1280 px page and consent copy reduced to tiny text that is impractical to read.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a device-width viewport and responsive typography with comfortable measure and minimum sizes.

findings.summary: The mobile experience does not reflow and has undersized targets.
findings.evidence: Viewport meta is width=1280 and the focus probe found multiple targets below 44x44 CSS pixels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, allow unrestricted zoom, reflow at 320 CSS pixels and enlarge touch targets.

findings.summary: The page logs a network error during normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a 401 response from /api/okonto/me in the browser console.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle anonymous account state without emitting a failed request or console error.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling blocks the back-forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener and reported BFCache restoration blocked in the main frame.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide or visibilitychange and verify BFCache restoration.

findings.summary: The fixed viewport signal undermines mobile friendliness.
findings.evidence: The homepage declares width=1280 rather than device-width, and the 360 px capture is a scaled desktop layout. All sampled links did have href values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a device-width viewport while retaining crawlable href links.

findings.summary: No sitemap was available at the conventional root URL.
findings.evidence: robots.txt returned successfully but /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404; canonical URLs were present on sampled pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks Open Graph share metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found one JSON-LD block but no og:* meta properties on the homepage; the article did expose JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata for the homepage and each content template.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but key security headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP or HSTS; the cookies probe found 18 cookies flagged insecure by the primitive, including multiple 400-day values.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and HSTS, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest suitable SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: The initial page load has an excessive tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 44 third-party origins and five known tracker domains; HAR attributed 256 of 262 requests and 3.69 MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit vendors, remove non-essential trackers and gate optional analytics and ad calls behind an informed choice.

findings.summary: The visible login entry provides no passkey or WebAuthn affordance.
findings.evidence: The homepage exposes a login button, but the rendered DOM and scripts inspected in the audit showed no user-facing passkey or WebAuthn path. No permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer conditional passkey sign-in and registration in the account flow while keeping permissions user-triggered.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP and HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and an appropriate origin-isolation strategy.

findings.summary: Most homepage editorial content is unavailable to non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 10% raw-to-rendered content coverage on the homepage, while the article template reached 79%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the homepage story feed and navigation so core news remains available without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually and structurally imbalanced.
findings.evidence: The bright yellow proceed button is paired with advanced settings, but no equally immediate reject-all action is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Present accept and reject-all at the same level and visual weight, with customisation secondary.

findings.summary: The search field lacks basic programmatic input assistance.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found one input with no label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; its visible focus outline was none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a real label or matching accessible name, input type=search, autocomplete intent and visible focus styling.

findings.summary: The subscription CTA does not disclose price or commitment before navigation.
findings.evidence: The first-view header shows only SUBSKRYBUJ, with no adjacent price, renewal or cancellation context.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise price and renewal context at the CTA and keep cancellation terms easy to find throughout checkout.

findings.summary: Image and media delivery is not sufficiently responsive.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 61 of 100 images without srcset and four below-fold images not lazy-loaded; HAR also loaded a 203 KB decorative MP4.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide responsive sources and sizes, lazy-load non-critical imagery and avoid loading decorative video before it is visible.

findings.summary: Large optional tracking and marketing workloads start on initial load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 118 scripts and 40 fetch/XHR requests; Lighthouse identified 603 KiB unused JavaScript and 200 ms blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional integrations until consent and visibility, batch telemetry and stop background work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party resources dominate the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 3.69 MB of 3.81 MB to non-main origins and the tracker probe observed 44 external origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable per-template third-party budgets and remove or conditionally load the largest vendors.

findings.summary: The homepage is weakly agent-readable and exposes no structured browser tools.
findings.evidence: Homepage non-JS content coverage was 10%; the probe found no WebMCP registration while the article template retained 79% content coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core feed semantics and expose safe search or article-discovery actions through WebMCP where useful.

findings.summary: The homepage has a disproportionately large in-memory footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contained 892,248 nodes and 48.37 MB self size for a news landing page; the DOM itself had about 1,504 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce eagerly loaded scripts, vendor SDKs and hidden UI trees, then set a heap budget for the homepage.
